subject: Linguistics
title: Sociolects
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sociolects usable.

hook.text: Teenagers and surgeons don't sound alike—and it's not just vocabulary. Entire speech styles differ.

buildup.text: Sociolects are language varieties linked to social groups—defined by class, age, or profession.

discovery.text: Doctors, lawyers, and gamers each develop specialized vocabulary and communication norms.

twist.text: Using a group's sociolect signals membership—and using it wrong exposes you as an outsider.

climax.text: Sociolects create in-group solidarity while simultaneously excluding non-members.

punchline.text: Speak like the group, and you belong to the group.

quiz.question: What defines a sociolect?
options: Speech variety linked to a social group
